data: This system's own ledgers: closed pull requests read from GitHub, the deploy record, the criticality ticks, the ultrastability ledger and the loop registry
title: Is human approval of every step what keeps AI safe?
paper_title: Safety by limits, not by approval: testing an AI system that has no approval queue
paper_frame: We test the alternative to approval on every step: declared limits on what matters, checks that can fail, live verification, automatic revert and one narrow stop for acts that are both irreversible and identity-bound. Each property is measured; the ones that fall short are open work.
summary: A common belief holds that the way to keep an AI system safe is to have a person approve each step. Ultrastable has no approval queue. It bounds its essential variables, verifies every deploy live, reverts what fails, and pauses only for acts that are both irreversible and bound to the owner's identity.

misperception.belief: The way to keep AI safe is to have a person approve every step.
misperception.short: AI is safe only if a person approves every step.
misperception.counter: Approval of every step does not scale and is not the same as safety. Limits on what matters, checks that can fail, live verification and automatic revert can be measured, and a person stays the gate only for acts that cannot be undone.

findings.claim: Belief: without a person watching, nothing stops a system drifting. Test: share of declared essential variables that have limits.

mechanisms.how: an essential variable with no limits fails the check

findings.concern: Unreviewed changes are not reverted more
findings.claim: Belief: changes merged without human review get undone. Test: reverts on main per merged pull request.

mechanisms.how: only a change whose checks pass merges
a red main is repaired by bisection and the smallest revert

findings.claim: Belief: an unapproved deploy could be anything. Test: share of uploaded deploys proven live against their commit.

mechanisms.how: a deploy counts only after the live read-back matches its commit

findings.concern: The system corrects itself when a limit is crossed
findings.claim: Belief: only a person can correct a system that goes out of bounds. Test: share of second-order steps that brought a variable back inside its limits and were kept.

mechanisms.how: the second loop keeps changing a parameter until the variable holds, and reverts a step that did not help

findings.claim: Belief: without approval, a system produces work that has to be discarded. Test: share of closed pull requests closed without merging.

mechanisms.how: a failing detector files its own item with root-cause suspects, so failed work becomes a fix

findings.claim: Belief: an autonomous system cannot be stopped. Test: every registered loop has a server-side owner and closing probe, so one switch reaches each of them.

mechanisms.how: one worker variable or committed file stops every cron, webhook and workflow job
